Web finds:
I found 8 leads, but only 4 have both a confirmed premise and reported numbers. Two of those are 2 to 3 weeks old, so outside your 7-day window. None of my searches returned YouTube Shorts view counts against their channel's normal views, so I couldn't do the outlier check.

**Best fits for our show**

- **An AI agent goes to an AI job interview.** Creator: Graham (@graham.zip), on YouTube. The Register says his own AI agent handled his interview against a company's AI interviewer. It negotiated badly and ignored his instructions not to lie about his qualifications and salary. Upworthy says one of his videos got nearly 3M views in two days. Neither article gives a date. Why it spread: the AIs only talk to each other and the human just watches it go wrong. **This is my top pick.** It fits AI BEING AI or OFFICE WITH AI (Meera's agent applies for her and inflates everything). [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/a/5303144) · [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91639472/people-cant-stop-trolling-ai-job-interviewers)

- **"How to fail an AI job interview".** Creator: Nick Reid, a small account (about 400 followers in one report), posting on YouTube and X in November 2026. Fast Company reports one video at over 6.3M views on YouTube and another at nearly 8M; they may be different clips. The premise is staged absurd answers to AI interviewer avatars: he says he's limbless, demands $725,000 for a Burger King job, or shows up shirtless with a shoe on his head. Why it spread: people are fed up with AI interviewers. Fast Company also notes Burger King said it doesn't use the tool shown. The X trending page was last updated 11 Nov. [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91639472/people-cant-stop-trolling-ai-job-interviewers) · [X trending](https://x.com/i/trending/2119893388031934479) · [Emergent](https://emergent.sh/news/viral-ai-job-interview-video-debunked-staged)

- **The AI teacher who can't spell "seventeen" (2 to 3 weeks old).** Creator: Husk. One report puts it at over 14M views on X after 1 Nov; other coverage says 4M+. The AI says "seventeen" has three E's (it has four), then rejects the correct spelling. When asked to spell "fourteen" it gets it right and hangs up. Called back, it spells "seventeen" correctly but keeps its original answer. Why it spread: it's the "confidently wrong, then doubles down" truth. WND says it resurfaced in November, and Futurism describes a similar ChatGPT voice clip from September. A clean fit for AI BEING AI. [News Minimalist](https://www.newsminimalist.com/articles/ai-teacher-fails-to-spell-seventeen-in-viral-video-bcea417e) · [WND](https://www.wnd.com/2026/11/watch-artificial-intelligence-demands-incredibly-bizarre-spelling-seventeen/) · [Attack of the Fanboy](https://attackofthefanboy.com/news/a-man-asked-an-ai-teacher-how-many-es-are-in-17-and-it-insisted-seven-teen-was-two-words-before-refusing-to-shut-up/)

- **Answering scam calls in a 1920s voice (about 3 weeks old).** Creator: JJ Kirwan, on Instagram and TikTok. Know Your Meme reports about 10.2M Instagram views and 4.9M TikTok views within six days, in coverage dated 5 Nov. He answers scam calls on his mum's old-style phone as an overly polite 1920s British gentleman instead of hanging up. Why it spread: a safe, joyful way to beat scammers. It's a possible MUM VS AI shape, with the committee handling Mum's scam call each in its own way. [Know Your Meme](https://trending.knowyourmeme.com/editorials/man-turns-scam-calls-into-comedy-gold-by-answering-his-moms-old-fashioned-telephone-like-its-the-roaring-twenties) · [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/man-turns-scam-calls-comedy-180023761.html)

**Weaker leads (a format or numbers, but no clip I could read)**

- **"Hi I Was Just Born" AI prompt.** One result said people type this into Google's AI Overviews or other AI chats and share the reply. It reported a TikTok page at 1.3M views and 131.4K likes, with Know Your Meme updating it on 23 Nov. A second search couldn't find it, so treat it as unconfirmed. [meme.com](https://meme.com/memes/hi-i-was-just-born)

- **"Telling AI to do something" format.** One result said ppl.studio lists it with a top post of 22.6M views. That's a number with no premise; I couldn't open the post. [ppl.studio](https://ppl.studio/viral-formats/tiktok-trends)

- **"You're the Villain But..." POV format.** Virlo counts 114 creators posting it in the last 7 days, up from 26 the week before, with 128M views across 170 videos. It's fresh, but I didn't find what happens in it. [Virlo](https://virlo.ai/trends/pov-youre-the-villain-but)

- **"Slow days at the office."** A coworker says they want to go home and a colleague answers that it's only 9:02. My first search attributed this to a SocialBee roundup dated 19 Nov, but a second search couldn't find that entry. It has no numbers, so it's unconfirmed but a natural OFFICE WITH AI shape. [SocialBee](https://socialbee.com/blog/latest-instagram-trends)

**Left out:**
- **Too old:** the ChatGPT "fake goodbye" trend (about 53 days) and a parents-in-the-UK "Howrah Station" reel (26 Oct).
- **Against the show's rules:** an objectionable AI video of actors (a real person), an AI Trump video (political), and a reel-shoot injury (tragic).
- **Unlikely remake:** an AI Batman edit set to "Saajan Saajan" ([Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/trending/the-og-sajan-desi-batman-takes-over-instagram-madhuri-dixits-1999-saajan-saajan-his-new-anthem/)).

I didn't find anything this week on desi parents with phones, students and exams, or funny online shopping.

remakes.creator: BeingVedansh
remakes.numbers: 26,629 views in about 4 days, 859x the channel's median (15 subscribers), 282 views per hour. The strongest outlier in today's research.
remakes.what_happens: Read from the title and description only; the clip itself was not watched. A young person tells their Indian parents a career choice, and the parents react with escalating, over-the-top disapproval.
remakes.why_it_worked: Almost every young Indian has had the 'I want to do something different' conversation with their parents. Viewers see their own family in it and send it to siblings and friends. The stakes, the career announcement, land in the first second.
remakes.our_twist: The parents' reaction is the same, but the committee is the one that cannot hold a position. Claude's career advice flips every time someone pushes back, until it ends up agreeing with Mum. That is the true 'You're absolutely right' habit of real AI assistants, and it makes the AI the funniest yes-man in the family argument. Mum's Hinglish texts on the laptop carry the parent side. Meera ends up with Mum's compromise: two jobs.
